source: Rudolf Steiner, For the Days of the Week (GA 245); English by Sophia Commons from the German original at anthroposophie.net

days.name: Right judgment
text: Make resolutions, even regarding the most trivial matters, only after full and well-founded deliberation. All thoughtless action and meaningless activity should be kept away from the soul. One should always have well-considered reasons for everything, and strictly refrain from doing anything for which there is no significant reason.
If one is convinced of the correctness of a decision one has made, one should hold fast to it with inner steadfastness. This judgment is not made dependent on likes and dislikes.

days.name: The right word
text: Only that which has sense and meaning should pass the lips of one who strives for higher development. All talking for the sake of talking, merely to pass the time, is harmful in this sense.

The ordinary kind of conversation, where a jumble of things is said, should be avoided; yet one must not cut oneself off from other people. It is precisely in such interaction that speech should gradually evolve toward significance. Answer everyone who speaks to you, thoughtfully and with consideration for every aspect. Never speak without a reason, and be ready to remain silent. Use neither too many nor too few words. First listen calmly, then process what has been heard.

days.name: The right deed
text: External actions should not be a source of disturbance to our fellow human beings. Whenever one is prompted by one's inner self (conscience) to act, carefully consider how best to respond for the good of the whole, for the lasting happiness of others, and for the sake of the eternal.
When acting on one's own initiative, thoroughly consider the consequences of one's actions beforehand.

days.name: The right standpoint
text: Live in harmony with nature and the spirit; do not lose oneself in the trivialities of outward life. Avoid anything that brings restlessness and haste into one's life.
Do nothing in haste, yet do not be sluggish. See life as a means for work and for higher development, and act accordingly.

days.name: Making the exercises a habit
text: Take care not to do anything beyond one's strength, yet also not to neglect anything that lies within it.

Look beyond the everyday and the immediate moment to set goals (ideals) connected with a human being's highest duties: for instance, wishing to develop oneself in the spirit of these exercises so as to be better able to help and advise others later on, even if not in the immediate future.

days.name: Right memory
text: Strive to learn as much as possible from life. Nothing passes us by without offering an opportunity to gather experiences useful for life. If one has done something incorrectly or imperfectly, this becomes an occasion to do something similar correctly later on.

When watching others act, observe them with a similar goal in mind (though not with unloving eyes), and do nothing without looking back on experiences that can aid one's decisions and actions. One can learn a great deal from every person, even from children, if one pays attention.

days.name: Right opinion
text: Pay attention to one's mental images (thoughts). Think only significant thoughts. Gradually learn to distinguish, within one's thoughts, the essential from the inessential, the eternal from the transient, and truth from mere opinion.

When listening to what others say, try to become completely still within and refrain from all assent, and especially from all disparaging judgment (criticism or rejection), even in one's thoughts and feelings.

daily.name: Right contemplation
text: Take a look inside yourself, if only for five minutes at the same time every day. Immerse yourself in yourself, carefully consult with yourself, examine and form your principles of life, go through your knowledge (or its opposite) in your mind, consider your duties, and reflect on the content and true purpose of life.

Be seriously dissatisfied with your own mistakes and imperfections; in a word, strive to find out what is essential and lasting, and seriously set yourself corresponding goals, for example virtues to be acquired. Do not think you have done something well, but always strive further, following the highest role models.
